Decide where to go: rank trip ideas with your group

Group chats are bad at choosing a destination: the first suggestion anchors everyone and quiet people don't vote. Send one link, let each person pick between pairs privately, and combine.

Why picking pairs works here

  • Each person weighs the same, however many questions they answered.
  • The agreement score tells you whether the group really wants the same thing or is split into camps, and the best-to-worst column shows which places are divisive.
  • No accounts, no app to install: it works in any phone browser.

What it doesn't do: It ranks what people would rather do, not what fits the budget or the dates. Take the clear losers off the list first if money or time rules them out.

Compared with what you'd use today

Polls in a group chat, shared spreadsheets, or trip-planning apps with voting. A poll picks a winner but hides how much people care. Pairwise picks give an order and show where people disagree.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
